title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Campania and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Campania's three DOCGs, Taurasi, Fiano di Avellino and Greco di Tufo, are all in Irpinia. Other names include Irpinia DOC, Falanghina del Sannio, Campi Flegrei, Lacryma Christi del Vesuvio, from Vesuvius' slopes, and Costa d'Amalfi. Riserva on Taurasi means at least four years of ageing.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Campania's food suits its wines: Fiano with buffalo mozzarella and seafood; Greco with fried fish and pasta with clams; Falanghina with pizza margherita; Taurasi with Neapolitan ragù, slow-cooked meat sauce, lamb and aged cheese. Serve whites at 10 to 12, Taurasi at 16 to 18, decanted.
steps.highlight: Mozzarella with Fiano, ragù with Taurasi

steps.explanation: Slow-cooked meat sauce suits Aglianico's tannin.

steps.body: Lacryma Christi, the tears of Christ, is a legendary name for wine from Vesuvius' slopes, red from Piedirosso and white from Coda di Volpe.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Campania's three DOCGs are all in Irpinia
Fiano suits mozzarella; Taurasi suits ragù
